lessons: Requisition review found the section 20 fence still too narrow, even after the plan edit that added stages.py and merge.py. The paved road is to fix the plan, then re-author the ticket. Retrying the authoring ticket alone cannot fix this.

compose_pipeline builds its own Registry(config) in stages.compose. A default that falls back to it is a forbidden dual path, so the shared payload must be a required parameter. That breaks unfenced callers in eval/shakeout/bench.py and eval/daemon_soak.py.
The required payload parameter also breaks unfenced test callers: tests/test_merge.py, tests/test_mergequeue.py and tests/test_daemon_composition.py.
Serve.compose and the Session/restart_session changes also reach unfenced callers: tests/test_serve.py and eval/daemon_soak.py. Only tests/test_restart_timers.py is fenced.

Plan fix: add every direct caller of compose_pipeline, Serve.compose and Session to section 20's provider-cooldown-failover hooks, as measured on-demand exceptions. The alternative is to choose a signature that forbids no existing caller. Then regenerate.

Keep the approved parts: registry suffix, edges, tiers, budgets, DATA_MARKER wording, measured headroom assertions, and the predecessor-test migrations in phase3_01, phase3_08 and phase4_01. Update the OWNERSHIP and ON_DEMAND tables to match the widened hooks.
reason: Section 20's fixed provider-cooldown-failover fence omits callers that the required shared-payload composition must change, so the ticket as written cannot be satisfied until the plan is fixed.
